title: Finite Q3 source-edge high-cutoff commutator stress
question: Does the source-edge graph commutator retain a cutoff-growing lower bound on explicit high-occupation Fock vectors when the target edge is kept fixed and the oscillator dimension is increased?

model.graph: the exact two-site Q3 target edge
model.high_core_vectors: tensor Fock vectors |d-1,d-1> and |d-1,0> in each d-dimensional truncation
model.diagnostic: the ratio ||[K_full,K_edge]psi||/||K_full psi|| and the global operator norm ||C||

adversarial_review.check: The linear inequality is checked only on the declared finite dimensions and explicit vectors; it is not asserted as an asymptotic theorem.
The high vectors are genuine basis vectors of each finite oscillator matrix; no untruncated CCR or continuum limit is substituted.
The source-edge weight is exactly the two-site onsite-plus-internal-bond weight; no external bonds are hidden in K_edge.
The commutator is evaluated after the full graph inverse; the form constant from EXP-001197 is not used to manufacture this lower bound.
The independent lane reconstructs the oscillator, two-site Hamiltonian and source-edge matrix from scratch.
A cutoff-growing sample rejects only the tested fixed graph-commutator route as a candidate uniform input; it does not reject cancellation-aware or state-weighted histories.
No common core, thermodynamic dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay conclusion follows.
R357 checks dimension, slope and scope arithmetic only; matrix norms and high-cutoff behavior remain Python evidence.

next_action: Treat the high-cutoff trend as a route-local boundary for a raw source-edge commutator coefficient. Replace it with a cancellation-aware or state-weighted history estimate whose coefficient is controlled on the common core, and require an analytic cutoff-uniform proof before any common-alpha promotion.

qft_interface.closed: A reproducible two-site Q3 high-cutoff stress shows an explicit high-occupation commutator ratio and its finite linear lower-bound diagnostic, independently reconstructed and Lean-bookkept.
qft_interface.open: An asymptotic theorem, source/volume/cutoff-uniform common-core estimate, cutoff removal, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 route evidence only; no heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite high-cutoff route stress. It is not a global no-go theorem or a QFT/Clay result.
no_overclaim: The sampled linear lower bound is finite and route-specific. It does not establish divergence in the untruncated theory or rule out other topologies.
